newsitem.title: USA: Lucent shrs up on strong Q2 earnings outlook.
newsitem.headline: Lucent shrs up on strong Q2 earnings outlook.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc shares bounced higher Thursday after the company told analysts it has cut internal costs and expects strong second-quarter sales in its software and wireless divisions.

Analysts said the telecommunications equipment company was riding an industry-wide wave in U.S. wireless expansion. Lucent also was a major beneficiary of telephone companies' upgrades in switch software.
"There is kind of a bonanza" across the industry, said Barry Sine, an analyst at SBC Warburg Inc.
Lucent shares were up 1-5/8 to 51-3/4 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said Lucent's streamlining efforts were especially noteworthy, citing a drop in selling, general and administrative (SGA) expenses and a cut in payroll costs.

"I am not reading a major revenue surprise into it. I am reading really a strong endorsement of Lucent management," Michael Schmidt, an analyst at CS First Boston, said after Lucent held a morning conference call.

Lucent chief financial officer Donald Peterson said second-quarter sales in the high-margin areas of software and wireless, as well as international strength, would boost earnings to $0.09-$0.10 per share on revenues of about $5.1 billion.
The First Call consensus estimate for the quarter is $0.04 per share.
Lucent did not break down the quarterly sales numbers during the conference call.
Sine said a contract signed by Lucent last July to outsource its daily information technology operations to International Business Machines Corp was paying off.

He said he expected SGA expenses to account for about 22 percent of fiscal 1997 revenues, down from 24.2 percent a year earlier, leading to savings of about $360 million after taxes, or $0.56 per share.
Analysts also said the change in the company's fiscal year, shifting the end of the year to September from December, helped sales in the second quarter.
"Lucent had the flexibility to not push as hard in December so that business could naturally flow into the March quarter," Schmidt said.

Analysts said Lucent was reaping the rewards of increased competition among phone companies who, in the aftermath of the U.S. Telecommunicatons Act, are eager to offer customers features such as call waiting and portability, which require upgraded switch software.
"The gross margins on the software upgrades are quite lucrative," said Neil Danzger, an analyst at Morgan Stanley.
Danzger said Lucent's outlook "bodes well for the industry," including competitors such as Northern Telecom Ltd, ADC Telecommunications Inc, Tellabs Inc and DSC Communications Corp.
NorTel shares were up 1/2 to 89-1/2 on the Toronto exchange. Tellab gained 1-5/8 to 35-5/8, DSC rose 1-5/8 to 20-1/4, and ADC gained 1-1/16 to 28-7/16.
